item.title: Central North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ACPN50 PHFO 261747
TWOCP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM HST Wed Aug 26 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Kure Atoll, and
on Tropical Storm Iselle, located well to the west of the southern
tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Western East Pacific:
An elongated, broad area of low pressure located well to the
east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands is producing disorganized
showers and thunderstorms. Environmental conditions appear conducive
for gradual development of this system, and a tropical depression is
likely to form late this week or early this weekend while the system
drifts to the northeast, then turns westward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...50 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south of the Hawaiian
Islands late this week or over the weekend. Some gradual development
is possible by early next week while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward, well south-southwest of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Kelly
NNNN

item.description:

BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Lala Advisory Number  58
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM HST Wed Aug 26 2026
 
...LALA EXPECTED TO BECOME A REMNANT LOW BY THE END OF THE WEEK...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 AM HST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...36.1N 178.3W
ABOUT 610 MI...985 KM NNW OF PEARL AND HERMES ATOLL
ABOUT 530 MI...855 KM N OF KURE ATOLL
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 320 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...999 MB...29.50 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM HST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was
located near latitude 36.1 North, longitude 178.3 West. Lala is
moving toward the northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h), with a turn toward 
the north-northwest expected through Thursday. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts.
Some weakening is forecast during the next 48 hours, and Lala is 
forecast to become a post-tropical remnant low by Thursday night. 
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles (185 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 999 mb (29.50 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Zelinsky

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 58
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Wed Aug 26 2026 
058 
WTPA42 PHFO 262032
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  58
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM HST Wed Aug 26 2026
 
Satellite imagery reveals little change in Lala’s convective 
structure over the last couple of hours. Subjective Dvorak intensity 
estimates from HFO and JTWC at 1800 UTC were 35 and 30 kt, 
respectively, while objective estimates ranged from 45-50 kt. Given 
the relatively steady nature of Lala’s appearance on satellite 
imagery since the last advisory, the initial intensity was held at 
40 kt. 
 
Lala’s speed remains slow, with an initial motion estimate of 320/4 
kt. A high pressure ridge centered to the storm’s east-northeast 
will drive a slow storm motion toward the north-northwest, before 
the system gradually turns more westward as it moves away from the 
ridge’s influence. Little change was made to the track forecast from 
the last advisory package, as models generally exhibited good 
agreement in the track while Lala remains tropical.

With the storm moving over gradually decreasing SSTs and 
increasing vertical wind shear, Lala is expected to become a 
post-tropical remnant low within the next 48 hours, right when the 
system is forecast to cross the international dateline. Changes to 
the intensity forecast were minimal, with the main adjustment being 
to show an earlier dissipation for Lala at 96 hours. This is sooner 
than the previous forecast, as global models generally depict the 
system becoming an open trough over the weekend.
